title.zh: 卷十七 魏書十七 張樂于張徐傳
title.en: Volume 17: Book of Wei 17 - Biographies of Zhang, Yue, Yu, Zhang, and Xu
title.raw: 卷十七 魏書十七 張樂于張徐傳 Volume 17: Book of Wei 17 - Biographies of Zhang, Yue, Yu, Zhang, and Xu

sentences.zh: 张辽字文远，雁门马邑人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Liao, courtesy name Wenyuan, was a man of Mayi in Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liao, whose courtesy name was Wenyuan, came from Mayi in Yanmen commandery.

sentences.zh: 本聂壹之后，以避怨变姓。

translations.literal: Originally he was a descendant of Nie Yi; to avoid resentment he changed his surname.
translations.idiomatic: He was descended from Nie Yi but had changed his family name to escape a blood feud.

sentences.zh: 少为郡吏。

translations.literal: In youth he was a clerk of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he served as a commandery clerk.

sentences.zh: 汉末，并州刺史丁原以辽武力过人，召为从事，使将兵诣京都。

translations.literal: At the end of Han, the Inspector of Bingzhou, Ding Yuan, because Liao's martial strength surpassed others, summoned him as an aide and ordered him to lead troops to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Han, Ding Yuan, inspector of Bingzhou, impressed by Zhang Liao's exceptional fighting ability, appointed him as an aide-de-camp and sent him at the head of troops to the capital.

sentences.zh: 何进遣诣河北募兵，得千餘人。

translations.literal: He Jin dispatched him to north of the Yellow River to recruit soldiers; he obtained more than a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He Jin sent him north of the river to raise troops, and he returned with over a thousand recruits.

sentences.zh: 还，进败，以兵属董卓。

translations.literal: Returning, He Jin had been defeated, and he attached his troops to Dong Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he came back, He Jin had already fallen, and Zhang Liao placed his command under Dong Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 卓败，以兵属吕布，迁骑都尉。

translations.literal: When Zhuo was defeated, he attached his troops to Lü Bu and was promoted to Colonel of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: After Dong Zhuo's downfall he joined Lü Bu's forces and was promoted to colonel of cavalry.

sentences.zh: 布为李傕所败，从布东奔徐州，领鲁相，时年二十八。

translations.literal: When Bu was defeated by Li Jue, he followed Bu fleeing east to Xu Province, served as chancellor of Lu, and at that time was twenty-eight years old.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Bu was routed by Li Jue, Zhang Liao followed him east into Xu Province, became administrator of Lu, and was twenty-eight at the time.

sentences.zh: 太祖破吕布於下邳，辽将其众降，拜中郎将，赐爵关内侯。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor defeated Lü Bu at Xiapi; Liao led his multitude in surrender, was appointed General of the Gentlemen of the Household, and was granted the noble rank of secondary marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Cao took Xiapi and broke Lü Bu, Zhang Liao brought his men over in submission and was named a general of the household and enfeoffed as a secondary marquis at court.

sentences.zh: 数有战功，迁裨将军。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he had merit in battle and was promoted to major general.
translations.idiomatic: He won distinction again and again in the field and rose to the rank of major general.

sentences.zh: 袁绍破，别遣辽定鲁国诸县。

translations.literal: When Yuan Shao was broken, separately he dispatched Liao to pacify the counties of the Lu princedom.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yuan Shao had been crushed, Cao Cao detached Zhang Liao to secure every county in the state of Lu.

sentences.zh: 与夏侯渊围昌豨於东海，数月粮尽，议引军还，辽谓渊曰：“数日已来，每行诸围，豨辄属目视辽。

translations.literal: Together with Xiahou Yuan he besieged Chang Xi in Donghai; after several months the provisions were exhausted, and they deliberated on withdrawing the army. Liao said to Yuan: "For several days now, whenever I have walked the various siege lines, Xi has always fixed his eyes on Liao.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Xiahou Yuan in besieging Chang Xi in Donghai; when months of campaigning had emptied the granaries and the generals talked of pulling back, Zhang Liao told Xiahou Yuan, "Lately, whenever I tour the perimeter, Chang Xi keeps his gaze fixed on me.

sentences.zh: 又其射矢更稀，此必豨计犹豫，故不力战。

translations.literal: Moreover his shooting of arrows has become rarer; this must be because Xi's plans are hesitant, therefore he does not fight hard.
translations.idiomatic: His archery has slackened as well; he must be torn about what to do next, which is why he will not commit to a full fight.

sentences.zh: 辽欲挑与语，傥可诱也？

translations.literal: Liao wishes to challenge him to speak; perhaps he can be enticed?
translations.idiomatic: I would like to draw him into conversation—there may be a way to coax him out.

sentences.zh: ”乃使谓豨曰：“公有命，使辽传之。

translations.literal: " Then he sent someone to say to Xi: "The lord has a command; he has ordered Liao to transmit it.
translations.idiomatic: " He then sent a messenger to Chang Xi: "Our lord has issued orders, and he has asked me to relay them to you.

sentences.zh: ”豨果下与辽语，辽为说“太祖神武，方以德怀四方，先附者受大赏”。

translations.literal: " Xi indeed came down and spoke with Liao, and Liao for him explained that "the Grand Progenitor is divinely martial and is just now by virtue cherishing the four quarters; those who attach first receive great rewards".
translations.idiomatic: " Chang Xi did come down to parley, and Zhang Liao told him that Cao Cao was a formidable leader who was winning the realm by moral authority and that those who submitted early would be richly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 豨乃许降。

translations.literal: Xi then promised to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Xi agreed to yield.

sentences.zh: 辽遂单身上三公山，入豨家，拜妻子。

translations.literal: Liao thereupon alone ascended Mount Sangong, entered Xi's house, and bowed to wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liao then went alone up Mount Sangong, walked into Chang Xi's home, and paid his respects to the man's wife and children.

sentences.zh: 豨欢喜，随诣太祖。

translations.literal: Xi was pleased and followed to go to the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Chang Xi accompanied him to Cao Cao's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣豨还，责辽曰：“此非大将法也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor sent Xi back and reproached Liao, saying: "This is not the method of a great general.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent Chang Xi back to his post and rebuked Zhang Liao: "That is not how a senior commander should behave.

sentences.zh: ”辽谢曰：“以明公威信著於四海，辽奉圣旨，豨必不敢害故也。

translations.literal: " Liao apologized, saying: "Because the enlightened lord's prestige and trust are manifest throughout the four seas, and Liao carried out the sage command, Xi certainly did not dare to harm; that is the reason.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Liao bowed and replied, "I knew your authority reaches every corner of the land and that I bore your written order, so Chang Xi would never have dared harm me.

sentences.zh: ”从讨袁谭、袁尚於黎阳，有功，行中坚将军。

translations.literal: " He followed in attacking Yuan Tan and Yuan Shang at Liyang, had merit, and acted as general of the central solid.
translations.idiomatic: " He took part in the campaign against Yuan Tan and Yuan Shang at Liyang, distinguished himself, and was given acting rank as general of the central corps.

sentences.zh: 从攻尚於鄴，尚坚守不下。

translations.literal: He followed in attacking Shang at Ye; Shang firmly defended and was not taken.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the assault on Ye, where Yuan Shang held the walls and could not be dislodged.

sentences.zh: 太祖还许，使辽与乐进拔阴安，徙其民河南。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor returned to Xu and ordered Liao together with Yue Jin to seize Yin'an and move its people south of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao withdrew to Xu, he sent Zhang Liao and Yue Jin to take Yin'an and resettle its population south of the river.

sentences.zh: 复从攻鄴，鄴破，辽别徇赵国、常山，招降缘山诸贼及黑山孙轻等。

translations.literal: Again he followed in attacking Ye; when Ye was broken, Liao separately campaigned through Zhao and Changshan, summoning to surrender the various bandits along the mountains and Sun Qing of the Black Mountain band, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He returned for the siege of Ye, and after the city fell he swept Zhao and Changshan on a separate line, bringing the mountain outlaws and Black Mountain leaders such as Sun Qing to terms.

sentences.zh: 从攻袁谭，谭破，别将徇海滨，破辽东贼柳毅等。

translations.literal: He followed in attacking Yuan Tan; when Tan was broken, as a separate general he campaigned along the seacoast and defeated the Liaodong bandits Liu Yi and others.
translations.idiomatic: He fought in the final campaign against Yuan Tan, then led a detached column along the coast and smashed coastal raiders from Liaodong led by Liu Yi.

sentences.zh: 还鄴，太祖自出迎辽，引共载，以辽为荡寇将军。

translations.literal: Returning to Ye, the Grand Progenitor himself came out to welcome Liao, led him to ride together in the same carriage, and appointed Liao general who sweeps away bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Ye, Cao Cao rode out in person to greet him, had him share his carriage, and named him general who sweeps away bandits.

sentences.zh: 复别击荆州，定江夏诸县，还屯临颍，封都亭侯。

translations.literal: Again separately he struck Jing Province, pacified the counties of Jiangxia, returned and garrisoned Linying, and was enfeoffed as marquis of the metropolitan village.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned again into Jingzhou, secured the Jiangxia counties, took station at Linying on his return, and received a village marquisate at the capital.

sentences.zh: 从征袁尚於柳城，卒与虏遇，辽劝太祖战，气甚奋，太祖壮之，自以所持麾授辽。

translations.literal: He followed in campaigning against Yuan Shang at Liucheng; suddenly they encountered the barbarians. Liao urged the Grand Progenitor to fight; his spirit was very aroused; the Grand Progenitor thought him brave and personally handed the banner he held to Liao.
translations.idiomatic: During the expedition against Yuan Shang at Liucheng they ran straight into the nomad host; Zhang Liao pressed Cao Cao to give battle, and his fervor so impressed Cao Cao that he passed him his own command banner.

sentences.zh: 遂击，大破之，斩单于蹋顿。

translations.literal: Thereupon they attacked, greatly defeated them, and beheaded the Shanyu Tadun.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked at once, shattered the enemy, and killed the chanyu Tadun.

sentences.zh: 〈《傅子》曰：太祖将征柳城，辽谏曰：“夫许，天子之会也。

translations.literal: 〈The Fu zi says: When the Grand Progenitor was about to campaign to Liucheng, Liao remonstrated, saying: "Now Xu is the assembly place of the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Fu zi records that when Cao Cao was preparing the Liucheng expedition, Zhang Liao urged him to reconsider: "Xu is where the emperor resides.

sentences.zh: 今天子在许，公远北征，若刘表遣刘备袭许，据之以号令四方，公之势去矣。

translations.literal: Now the Son of Heaven is at Xu; the lord campaigns far to the north; if Liu Biao dispatches Liu Bei to raid Xu, occupies it, and by it issues commands to the four quarters, the lord's situation will be gone.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign is at Xu while you march deep into the north; if Liu Biao sent Liu Bei to strike the capital, seize it, and issue orders from there, your position would collapse.

sentences.zh: ”太祖策表必不能任备，遂行也。〉

translations.literal: " The Grand Progenitor calculated that Biao certainly could not employ Bei, and thereupon proceeded.〉
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao judged that Liu Biao would never give Liu Bei real authority, and went ahead with the campaign anyway.〉

sentences.zh: 时荆州未定，复遣辽屯长社。

translations.literal: At that time Jing Province was not yet settled, and again he dispatched Liao to garrison Changshe.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jingzhou was still unsettled, Cao Cao again posted Zhang Liao at Changshe.

sentences.zh: 临发，军中有谋反者，夜惊乱起火，一军尽扰。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure, in the army there were those who plotted rebellion; in the night alarm and confusion broke out and fire arose, and the whole army was thrown into turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: On the night before the march, mutineers set fires and panic spread until the entire camp was in chaos.

sentences.zh: 辽谓左右曰：“勿动。

translations.literal: Liao said to those at his side: "Do not move.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liao told his attendants, "Stay where you are.

sentences.zh: 是不一营尽反，必有造变者，欲以动乱人耳。

translations.literal: This is not that every camp has all rebelled; there must be those who made the disturbance, intending by it to move and disorder the people, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: This cannot be a general mutiny; someone has started trouble on purpose to stampede the ranks.

sentences.zh: ”乃令军中，其不反者安坐。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he ordered in the army that those who were not rebelling should sit peacefully.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered every loyal soldier to sit quietly in place.

sentences.zh: 辽将亲兵数十人，中陈而立。

translations.literal: Liao led several tens of personal soldiers and stood in the center of the formation.
translations.idiomatic: He took several dozen bodyguards and planted himself in the middle of the formation.

sentences.zh: 有顷定，即得首谋者杀之。

translations.literal: After a while it was settled, and immediately they obtained the chief plotter and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Order returned quickly; the ringleaders were seized and executed at once.

sentences.zh: 陈兰、梅成以氐六县叛，太祖遣于禁、臧霸等讨成，辽督张郃、牛盖等讨兰。

translations.literal: Chen Lan and Mei Cheng with the six Di counties rebelled; the Grand Progenitor dispatched Yu Jin, Zang Ba, and others to attack Cheng, and Liao supervised Zhang He, Niu Gai, and others to attack Lan.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Lan and Mei Cheng revolted with six Di counties, Cao Cao sent Yu Jin and Zang Ba against Mei Cheng while Zhang Liao, directing Zhang He and Niu Gai, moved against Chen Lan.

sentences.zh: 成伪降禁，禁还。

translations.literal: Cheng feigned surrender to Jin, and Jin returned.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Cheng tricked Yu Jin with a false surrender, and Yu Jin withdrew.

sentences.zh: 成遂将其众就兰，转入灊山。

translations.literal: Cheng thereupon led his multitude to join Lan and turned and entered the Qian mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Cheng then marched his men to Chen Lan's side, and both withdrew into the Qian range.

sentences.zh: 灊中有天柱山，高峻二十餘里，道险狭，步径裁通，兰等壁其上。

translations.literal: Within Qian there is Mount Tianzhu, lofty and steep for more than twenty li; the road is perilous and narrow, the foot path barely passable, and Lan and others fortified the heights above.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the range rises Mount Tianzhu, more than twenty li of sheer height along trails so treacherous and narrow that men could barely edge through; Chen Lan's men held the crest.

sentences.zh: 辽欲进，诸将曰：“兵少道险，难用深入。

translations.literal: Liao wished to advance; the various generals said: "The troops are few and the road perilous; it is difficult to use deep penetration.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liao wanted to push on, but his officers said, "We are outnumbered and the defiles are deadly; a deep thrust would be reckless.

sentences.zh: ”辽曰：“此所谓一与一，勇者得前耳。

translations.literal: " Liao said: "This is what is called one against one— the brave one gets to go forward, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Liao replied, "They call it even odds: courage decides who breaks through.

sentences.zh: ”遂进到山下安营，攻之，斩兰、成首，尽虏其众。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he advanced to below the mountain, encamped, attacked them, beheaded Lan and Cheng, and completely captured their multitude.
translations.idiomatic: " He camped at the foot of the mountain, stormed the heights, beheaded Chen Lan and Mei Cheng, and took their entire force prisoner.

sentences.zh: 太祖论诸将功，曰：“登天山，履峻险，以取兰、成，荡寇功也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor assessed the merit of the various generals and said: "To ascend Mount Tian, tread perilous steepness, and thereby take Lan and Cheng is the merit of the general who sweeps away bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao summed up the campaign: "Scaling Tianzhu and forcing those cliffs to bring down Chen Lan and Mei Cheng is exactly the work expected of the general who sweeps away bandits.

sentences.zh: ”增邑，假节。

translations.literal: " His fief was increased, and he was granted the credential insignia.
translations.idiomatic: " His fief was enlarged and he received the imperial baton of authority.

sentences.zh: 太祖既征孙权还，使辽与乐进、李典等将七千餘人屯合肥。

translations.literal: After the Grand Progenitor had campaigned against Sun Quan and returned, he ordered Liao together with Yue Jin, Li Dian, and others to lead more than seven thousand men and garrison Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao returned from his expedition against Sun Quan, he left Zhang Liao, Yue Jin, and Li Dian in Hefei with a garrison of more than seven thousand men.

sentences.zh: 太祖征张鲁，教与护军薛悌，署函边曰“贼至乃发”。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor campaigned against Zhang Lu; he gave instructions to the army protector Xue Ti and wrote on the edge of the sealed box "open when the bandits arrive".
translations.idiomatic: On setting out against Zhang Lu, Cao Cao handed sealed orders to the army protector Xue Ti with the note on the envelope, "Break the seal only when the enemy appears.

sentences.zh: 俄而权率十万众围合肥，乃共发教，教曰：“若孙权至者，张、李将军出战；

translations.literal: Shortly Quan led a hundred thousand multitude to besiege Hefei; thereupon together they opened the instructions; the instructions said: "If Sun Quan arrives, Generals Zhang and Li are to go out and fight;
translations.idiomatic: Soon Sun Quan arrived with a host of one hundred thousand to invest Hefei; the defenders opened the letter together. It read, "If Sun Quan comes in person, Generals Zhang and Li shall sortie;

sentences.zh: 乐将军守护军，勿得与战。

translations.literal: General Yue is to guard the army protector and must not join battle.
translations.idiomatic: General Yue is to stay with the army protector and must not engage.

sentences.zh: ”诸将皆疑。

translations.literal: " The various generals all doubted.
translations.idiomatic: " The commanders were baffled.

sentences.zh: 辽曰：“公远征在外，比救至，彼破我必矣。

translations.literal: Liao said: "The lord is on a distant expedition; compared to when relief arrives, they will certainly break us.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liao said, "Our lord is far away; if we wait for reinforcements, the enemy will have crushed us long before help arrives.

sentences.zh: 是以教指及其未合逆击之，折其盛势，以安众心，然后可守也。

translations.literal: Therefore the instruction points to striking them in reverse before they have fully united, breaking their flourishing momentum, thereby to settle the hearts of the multitude, and afterward one can defend.
translations.idiomatic: The orders tell us to hit them before their siege lines close, blunt their momentum, steady the troops, and only then think about holding the walls.

sentences.zh: 成败之机，在此一战，诸君何疑？

translations.literal: The pivot of success or defeat is in this one battle; why do you gentlemen doubt?
translations.idiomatic: Victory or ruin turns on this single fight—why hesitate?

sentences.zh: ”李典亦与辽同。

translations.literal: " Li Dian also agreed with Liao.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Dian sided with Zhang Liao.

sentences.zh: 於是辽夜募敢从之士，得八百人，椎牛飨将士，明日大战。

translations.literal: Thereupon Liao by night recruited dare-to-follow soldiers, obtained eight hundred men, slaughtered cattle and feasted officers and troops, and the next day there was a great battle.
translations.idiomatic: That night Zhang Liao enlisted eight hundred volunteers, slaughtered oxen for a feast, and at dawn led them into a major attack.

sentences.zh: 平旦，辽被甲持戟，先登陷陈，杀数十人，斩二将，大呼自名，冲垒入，至权麾下。

translations.literal: At dawn Liao donned armor, grasped a halberd, was first to ascend and break the formation, killed several tens of men, beheaded two generals, loudly shouted his own name, charged the ramparts and entered, reaching to beneath Quan's banner.
translations.idiomatic: At first light he armored himself, seized a halberd, spearheaded the charge, cut down dozens of men and two enemy commanders, roared his own name, burst through the stockade, and drove straight to Sun Quan's command post.

sentences.zh: 权大惊，众不知所为，走登高冢，以长戟自守。

translations.literal: Quan was greatly alarmed; the multitude did not know what to do; they fled and climbed a high mound and with long halberds defended themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan was terrified; his men froze, then fled to a burial mound and tried to shield him with long halberds.

sentences.zh: 辽叱权下战，权不敢动，望见辽所将众少，乃聚围辽数重。

translations.literal: Liao shouted at Quan to come down and fight; Quan did not dare move; seeing that the multitude Liao led was few, then they gathered and surrounded Liao in several layers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liao bellowed for Sun Quan to come down and fight; Sun Quan stayed frozen on the knoll, but when he saw how few Zhang Liao's men were he ordered ring after ring of troops to close around them.

sentences.zh: 辽左右麾围，直前急击，围开，辽将麾下数十人得出，餘众号呼曰：“将军弃我乎！

translations.literal: Liao to left and right gestured the encirclement, went straight forward and struck urgently; the encirclement opened, and Liao leading several tens of men under his command was able to get out; the remaining multitude cried out, saying: "Has the general abandoned us!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liao wheeled his men and slammed forward until the ring broke; he broke out with several dozen followers, while those left inside screamed, "General, are you leaving us behind?

sentences.zh: ”辽复还突围，拔出餘众。

translations.literal: " Liao again returned, broke the encirclement, and pulled out the remaining multitude.
translations.idiomatic: " He wheeled back, tore through the encirclement again, and led the rest of his men out.

sentences.zh: 权人马皆披靡，无敢当者。

translations.literal: Quan's men and horses all scattered; there was none who dared withstand him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan's army broke and scattered; no one dared stand in his way.

sentences.zh: 自旦战至日中，吴人夺气，还修守备，众心乃安，诸将咸服。

translations.literal: From dawn they fought until midday; the men of Wu lost their spirit; returning they repaired defensive preparations, and the hearts of the multitude were then settled; the various generals all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The fighting ran from dawn until noon, shattering Wu's morale; when the defenders withdrew behind the walls and shored up the defenses, the army's nerve returned and every general acknowledged Zhang Liao's leadership.

sentences.zh: 权守合肥十餘日，城不可拔，乃引退。

translations.literal: Quan guarded Hefei more than ten days; the city could not be taken; thereupon he led a withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan kept Hefei under siege for ten-odd days but could not storm it and finally drew off.

sentences.zh: 辽率诸军追击，几复获权。

translations.literal: Liao led the various armies in pursuit and nearly again captured Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liao pursued with the garrison troops and nearly took Sun Quan himself.

sentences.zh: 太祖大壮辽，拜征东将军。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor greatly thought Liao brave and appointed him general who campaigns east.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao was deeply impressed and promoted him to general who campaigns east.

sentences.zh: 〈孙盛曰；

translations.literal: 〈Sun Sheng says;
translations.idiomatic: 〈Sun Sheng remarks:

sentences.zh: 夫兵固诡道，奇正相资，若乃命将出征，推毂委权，或赖率然之形，或凭掎角之势，群帅不和，则弃师之道也。

translations.literal: Now warfare is indeed the way of deceit; the extraordinary and the regular mutually assist. As for ordering a general to go out on campaign, pushing the chariot shaft and entrusting authority, sometimes one relies on the form of sudden spontaneity, sometimes one depends on the momentum of pincer horns; if the host of commanders is not harmonious, that is the way to abandon the army.
translations.idiomatic: War is the art of deception, where surprise and straight fighting support each other. When a ruler sends a general forth, hands him full authority, and counts on either lightning opportunism or coordinated pincers, discord among the commanders is the surest way to lose an army.

sentences.zh: 至於合肥之守，县弱无援，专任勇者则好战生患，专任怯者则惧心难保。

translations.literal: As for the defense of Hefei, suspended weak without aid, if one solely employs the brave then fondness of battle produces disaster; if one solely employs the timid then fearful hearts are hard to preserve.
translations.idiomatic: Hefei's garrison was isolated, outnumbered, and without relief: put only daredevils in charge and reckless fighting becomes a liability; put only timid men in charge and fear will undo the defense.

sentences.zh: 且彼众我寡，必怀贪墯；

translations.literal: Moreover they are many and we are few; they are sure to harbor greed and sloth;
translations.idiomatic: The enemy outnumbers us, which invites complacency and greed;

sentences.zh: 以致命之兵，击贪墯之卒，其势必胜；

translations.literal: using troops who stake their lives to strike soldiers who are greedy and slothful, the situation is sure to be victory;
translations.idiomatic: pit troops ready to die against an overconfident horde, and the odds favor victory;

sentences.zh: 胜而后守，守则必固。

translations.literal: after victory then defend, and in defending one is sure to be firm.
translations.idiomatic: win that first clash, then fall back on the walls, and the defense will hold.

sentences.zh: 是以魏武推选方员，参以同异，为之密教，节宣其用；

translations.literal: Therefore Wei Wu selected and advanced the square and the round, mixed same and different, for them made secret instructions, and moderated and spread their use;
translations.idiomatic: That is why Cao Cao matched bold commanders with cautious ones, blended divergent temperaments, and issued sealed instructions that timed each man's role to perfection;

sentences.zh: 事至而应，若合符契，妙矣夫！〉

translations.literal: when the affair arrived they responded, as if matching tallies and contracts—wonderful indeed!〉
translations.idiomatic: when the crisis came each piece of the plan snapped into place like matching halves of a tally—masterful!〉

sentences.zh: 建安二十一年，太祖复征孙权，到合肥，循行辽战处，叹息者良久。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Jian'an, the Grand Progenitor again campaigned against Sun Quan; arriving at Hefei, he walked through the places of Liao's battle and sighed for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 21 Cao Cao marched against Sun Quan again; when he reached Hefei he walked the ground of Zhang Liao's battle and stood there sighing for a long while.

sentences.zh: 乃增辽兵，多留诸军，徙屯居巢。

translations.literal: Thereupon he increased Liao's troops, left many of the various armies, and moved the garrison to Juhao.
translations.idiomatic: He enlarged Zhang Liao's command, kept substantial forces in the area, and shifted the main camp to Juhao.

sentences.zh: 乐进字文谦，阳平卫国人也。

translations.literal: Yue Jin, courtesy name Wenqian, was a man of Weiguo in Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Jin, courtesy name Wenqian, was a native of Wei county in Yangping.

sentences.zh: 容貌短小，以胆烈从太祖，为帐下吏。

translations.literal: His appearance was short in stature; by courage and fierceness he followed the Grand Progenitor and was a clerk under the tent.
translations.idiomatic: He was short of stature but fierce in spirit; he joined Cao Cao's staff as a brave attendant.

sentences.zh: 遣还本郡募兵，得千餘人，还为军假司马、陷陈都尉。

translations.literal: He was sent back to his native commandery to recruit soldiers, obtained more than a thousand men, returned and became acting major of the army and colonel who breaks the formation.
translations.idiomatic: Sent home to raise troops, he brought back more than a thousand men and was promoted to acting major and colonel of the assault corps.

sentences.zh: 从击吕布於濮阳，张超於雍丘，桥昽於苦，皆先登有功，封广昌亭侯。

translations.literal: He followed in striking Lü Bu at Puyang, Zhang Chao at Yongqiu, and Qiao Rui at Ku; in all he was first to ascend and had merit, and was enfeoffed as marquis of the Guangchang village.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Lü Bu at Puyang, Zhang Chao at Yongqiu, and Qiao Rong at Ku, earning distinction as first on the wall each time, and received a village marquisate at Guangchang.

sentences.zh: 从征张绣於安众，围吕布於下邳，破别将，击眭固於射犬，攻刘备於沛，皆破之，拜讨寇校尉。

translations.literal: He followed in campaigning against Zhang Xiu at Anzhong, besieged Lü Bu at Xiapi, broke a separate general, struck Sui Gu at Shequan, attacked Liu Bei at Pei; in all he defeated them and was appointed colonel who attacks bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Anzhong campaign against Zhang Xiu, the Xiapi siege of Lü Bu, a separate action that routed an enemy column, the Shequan fight against Sui Gu, and the Pei assault on Liu Bei, winning every engagement and gaining the rank of colonel who attacks bandits.

sentences.zh: 渡河攻获嘉，还，从击袁绍於官渡，力战，斩绍将淳于琼。

translations.literal: He crossed the Yellow River and attacked Huojia, returned, followed in striking Yuan Shao at Guandu, fought hard, and beheaded Shao's general Chunyu Qiong.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the river to storm Huojia, then fought Yuan Shao at Guandu, where he killed the general Chunyu Qiong in heavy combat.

sentences.zh: 从击谭、尚於黎阳，斩其大将严敬，行游击将军。

translations.literal: He followed in striking Tan and Shang at Liyang, beheaded their great general Yan Jing, and acted as general of mobile strike.
translations.idiomatic: At Liyang he helped crush Yuan Tan and Yuan Shang, slew their champion Yan Jing, and received acting appointment as general of mobile strike.

sentences.zh: 别击黄巾，破之，定乐安郡。

translations.literal: Separately he struck the Yellow Turbans, defeated them, and pacified the commandery of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: On a separate mission he broke the Yellow Turbans and secured Le'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 从围鄴，鄴定，从击袁谭於南皮，先登，入谭东门。

translations.literal: He followed in besieging Ye; when Ye was settled, he followed in striking Yuan Tan at Nanpi, was first to ascend, and entered Tan's east gate.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the siege of Ye, then fought Yuan Tan at Nanpi, where he was first through the east gate.

sentences.zh: 谭败，别攻雍奴，破之。

translations.literal: When Tan was defeated, separately he attacked Yongnu and defeated it.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Tan's defeat he took Yongnu in a separate attack.

sentences.zh: 建安十一年，太祖表汉帝，称进及于禁、张辽曰：“武力既弘，计略周备，质忠性一，守执节义，每临战攻，常为督率，奋强突固，无坚不陷，自援枹鼓，手不知倦。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Jian'an, the Grand Progenitor memorialized the Han emperor, praising Jin together with Yu Jin and Zhang Liao, saying: "Their martial power is already vast, their plans and strategies thorough and complete, their substance loyal and nature unified, they preserve and hold to integrity and righteousness; whenever they face battle and attack, they always act as overseers and leaders, exerting strength and bursting solid positions, no strong point they do not take; they themselves grasp the drumsticks and beat the drums, and their hands do not know weariness.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 11 Cao Cao memorialized the Han throne, commending Yue Jin with Yu Jin and Zhang Liao: "These officers combine great martial prowess with careful planning, unwavering loyalty, and steadfast honor. In every action they lead from the front, shatter the toughest defenses, beat the war drums themselves, and never tire.

sentences.zh: 又遣别征，统御师旅，抚众则和，奉令无犯，当敌制决，靡有遗失。

translations.literal: Moreover when separately dispatched on campaign, commanding and controlling armies and brigades, in soothing the multitude they are harmonious, in receiving orders they commit no violations, when facing the enemy they decide measures, and there is nothing missed.
translations.idiomatic: Detached commands find them able to control large forces, keep the ranks steady, obey orders to the letter, and make the right call under fire without fault.

sentences.zh: 论功纪用，宜各显宠。

translations.literal: In assessing merit and recording employment, it is fitting that each receive manifest favor.
translations.idiomatic: Their records of service merit explicit rewards.

sentences.zh: ”於是禁为虎威；

translations.literal: " Thereupon Jin became tiger might;
translations.idiomatic: " Yu Jin was therefore named general of tiger might;

sentences.zh: 进，折冲；

translations.literal: Jin, ram that breaks the charge;
translations.idiomatic: Yue Jin, general who breaks the charge;

sentences.zh: 辽，荡寇将军。

translations.literal: Liao (was made) general who sweeps away bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liao was named general who sweeps away bandits.

sentences.zh: 进别征高幹，从北道入上党，回出其后。

translations.literal: Jin separately campaigned against Gao Gan, entered Shangdang by the northern route, and circled to come out behind him.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Jin campaigned separately against Gao Gan, entered Shangdang by the northern road, and swung around onto his rear.

sentences.zh: 幹等还守壶关，连战斩首。

translations.literal: Gan and others returned to defend Huguan; in successive battles heads were cut.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gan fell back on Huguan, where Yue Jin fought a series of actions and piled up beheadings.

sentences.zh: 幹坚守未下，会太祖自征之，乃拔。

translations.literal: Gan firmly defended and was not taken; when it happened that the Grand Progenitor personally campaigned against him, then it was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gan held out until Cao Cao arrived in person and the fortress finally fell.

sentences.zh: 太祖征管承，军淳于，遣进与李典击之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor campaigned against Guan Cheng, army at Chunyu, and dispatched Jin together with Li Dian to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunyu campaign against Guan Cheng, Cao Cao sent Yue Jin and Li Dian against him.

sentences.zh: 承破走，逃入海岛，海滨平，荆州未服，遣屯阳翟。

translations.literal: Cheng was broken and fled, escaping into sea islands; the seacoast was pacified; Jing Province had not submitted; he was dispatched to garrison Yangzhai.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Cheng was routed and fled to offshore islands; with the coast quiet but Jingzhou still defiant, Yue Jin was posted to Yangzhai.

sentences.zh: 后从平荆州，留屯襄阳，击关羽、苏非等，皆走之，南郡诸郡山谷蛮夷诣进降。

translations.literal: Afterward he followed in pacifying Jing Province, remained garrisoned at Xiangyang, struck Guan Yu, Su Fei, and others, all routed them, and the barbarians of the mountains and valleys of the various commanderies of Nan commandery came to Jin to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He then helped subdue Jingzhou and was left to hold Xiangyang, where he drove off Guan Yu and Su Fei and brought the hill tribes of Nan commandery in to surrender to him.

sentences.zh: 又讨刘备临沮长杜普、旌阳长梁大，皆大破之。

translations.literal: Again he attacked Liu Bei's Linju magistrate Du Pu and Jingyang magistrate Liang Da, and in all greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He also campaigned against Liu Bei's district magistrates Du Pu of Linju and Liang Da of Jingyang and crushed both.

sentences.zh: 后从征孙权，假进节。

translations.literal: Afterward he followed in campaigning against Sun Quan, and Jin was lent the credential insignia.
translations.idiomatic: On a later expedition against Sun Quan he was granted the imperial baton.

sentences.zh: 太祖还，留进与张辽、李典屯合肥，增邑五百，并前凡千二百户。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor returned, left Jin together with Zhang Liao and Li Dian to garrison Hefei, increased his fief by five hundred households, and together with the previous total it came to one thousand two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao withdrew, he left Yue Jin with Zhang Liao and Li Dian at Hefei, adding five hundred households to his fief for a total of twelve hundred.

sentences.zh: 以进数有功，分五百户，封一子列侯；

translations.literal: Because Jin repeatedly had merit, five hundred households were divided off and one son was enfeoffed as full marquis;
translations.idiomatic: For his repeated victories he was awarded another five hundred households and a full marquisate for one of his sons;

sentences.zh: 进迁右将军。

translations.literal: Jin was promoted to general of the right.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Jin was promoted to general of the right.

sentences.zh: 建安二十三年薨，谥曰威侯。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Jian'an he died; his posthumous title was Marquis Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jian'an 23 and was posthumously titled Marquis Wei, "the Formidable."

sentences.zh: 子綝嗣。

translations.literal: The son Chen inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yue Chen inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 綝果毅有父风，官至扬州刺史。

translations.literal: Chen was resolute and decisive and had his father's manner; his office reached to Inspector of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Chen was as resolute as his father and rose to inspector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 诸葛诞反，掩袭杀綝，诏悼惜之，追赠卫尉，谥曰愍侯。

translations.literal: When Zhuge Dan rebelled, he launched a surprise attack and killed Chen; an edict mourned and pitied him, posthumously gifted him Minister of the Guards, and his posthumous title was Marquis Min.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Dan revolted he ambushed and killed Yue Chen; the court issued an edict of regret, posthumously named him minister of the guards, and gave him the posthumous title Marquis Min, "the Pitiable."

sentences.zh: 子肇嗣。

translations.literal: The son Zhao inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yue Zhao succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 于禁字文则，泰山钜平人也。

translations.literal: Yu Jin, courtesy name Wenze, was a man of Juping in Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin, courtesy name Wenze, was a native of Juping in Taishan commandery.

sentences.zh: 黄巾起，鲍信招合徒众，禁附从焉。

translations.literal: When the Yellow Turbans arose, Bao Xin recruited and assembled followers, and Jin attached himself and followed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow Turban rebellion broke out, he joined the force that Bao Xin raised.

sentences.zh: 及太祖领兗州，禁与其党俱诣为都伯，属将军王朗。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor took charge of Yan Province, Jin together with his faction all went and became company chiefs, subordinate to General Wang Lang.
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Cao took Yanzhou, Yu Jin and his comrades enlisted as company commanders under General Wang Lang.

sentences.zh: 朗异之，荐禁才任大将军。

translations.literal: Lang thought him extraordinary and recommended Jin's talent as fit for grand general.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang was impressed and recommended him as material for high command.

sentences.zh: 太祖召见与语，拜军司马，使将兵诣徐州，攻广威，拔之，拜陷陈都尉。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor summoned him for an audience and conversed with him, appointed him major of the army, ordered him to lead troops to Xu Province, attacked Guangwei, took it, and appointed him colonel who breaks the formation.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao received him in audience, named him army major, sent him to Xu Province, where he took Guangwei by storm, then promoted him to colonel of the assault corps.

sentences.zh: 从讨吕布於濮阳，别破布二营於城南，又别将破高雅於须昌。

translations.literal: He followed in attacking Lü Bu at Puyang, separately broke two of Bu's camps south of the city, and again as a separate general defeated Gao Ya at Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Lü Bu at Puyang, destroyed two of Lü Bu's camps south of the walls on a separate thrust, and later routed Gao Ya at Xuchang as detached commander.

sentences.zh: 从攻寿张、定陶、离狐，围张超於雍丘，皆拔之。

translations.literal: He followed in attacking Shouzhang, Dingtao, and Lihu, besieged Zhang Chao at Yongqiu, and in all took them.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the attacks on Shouzhang, Dingtao, and Lihu and the siege of Zhang Chao at Yongqiu, capturing every objective.

sentences.zh: 从征黄巾刘辟、黄邵等，屯版梁，邵等夜袭太祖营，禁帅麾下击破之，斩

translations.literal: He followed in campaigning against the Yellow Turbans Liu Pi, Huang Shao, and others; they garrisoned Banliang; Shao and others by night raided the Grand Progenitor's camp; Jin leading those under his command defeated them and struck down
translations.idiomatic: While campaigning against the Yellow Turban leaders Liu Pi and Huang Shao, he was at Banliang when Huang Shao raided Cao Cao's camp by night; Yu Jin led his men to repulse the attack and struck down

translations.literal: (Pi) — interlinear gloss supplying the name 辟 for Liu Pi.
translations.idiomatic: (The character 辟 is inserted here in the text as a gloss on 刘辟.)

sentences.zh: 邵等，尽降其众。

translations.literal: Shao and the others, and completely caused their multitude to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Shao and the rest of the band, then accepted the surrender of their entire following.

sentences.zh: 迁平虏校尉。

translations.literal: He was promoted to colonel who pacifies captives.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to colonel who pacifies barbarians.

sentences.zh: 从围桥蕤於苦，斩蕤等四将。

translations.literal: He followed in besieging Qiao Rui at Ku, beheaded Rui and four generals.
translations.idiomatic: At the siege of Qiao Rui at Ku he killed Rui and four other enemy generals.

sentences.zh: 从至宛，降张绣。

translations.literal: He followed to Wan and Zhang Xiu surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the army to Wan, where Zhang Xiu submitted.

sentences.zh: 绣复叛，太祖与战不利，军败，还舞阴。

translations.literal: Xiu again rebelled; the Grand Progenitor fought him with unfavorable outcome, the army was defeated, and returned to Wuyin.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Xiu rebelled again, Cao Cao was beaten in the field and fell back to Wuyin.

sentences.zh: 是时军乱，各间行求太祖，禁独勒所将数百人，且战且引，虽有死伤不相离。

translations.literal: At that time the army was in disorder; each by separate routes sought the Grand Progenitor; Jin alone restrained those he led, several hundred men, fighting while withdrawing; although there were deaths and wounds they did not separate from one another.
translations.idiomatic: In the rout men scattered to find Cao Cao, but Yu Jin alone held several hundred troops together, fighting a steady retreat so that even under casualties no one broke ranks.

sentences.zh: 虏追稍缓，禁徐整行队，鸣鼓而还。

translations.literal: The enemy pursuit gradually slackened; Jin slowly set in order the marching ranks, beat the drums, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the pursuit slackened he re-formed the column, beat the drums, and marched back in good order.

sentences.zh: 未至太祖所，道见十餘人被创裸走，禁问其故，曰：“为青州兵所劫。

translations.literal: Before reaching the Grand Progenitor's place, on the road he saw more than ten men wounded and naked fleeing; Jin asked the reason, and they said: "We were plundered by Qingzhou troops.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached Cao Cao he met a dozen wounded men fleeing naked; they told him the Qingzhou soldiers had robbed them.

sentences.zh: ”初，黄巾降，号青州兵，太祖宽之，故敢因缘为略。

translations.literal: " At first, when the Yellow Turbans surrendered, they were called Qingzhou troops; the Grand Progenitor treated them leniently, therefore they dared by the opportunity to commit pillage.
translations.idiomatic: " Former Yellow Turbans had been enrolled as the Qingzhou corps, and Cao Cao's leniency had emboldened them to loot.

sentences.zh: 禁怒，令其众曰：“青州兵同属曹公，而还为贼乎！

translations.literal: Jin was angry and ordered his multitude, saying: "The Qingzhou troops likewise belong to Lord Cao—would you turn and become bandits!
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin angrily told his men, "Those Qingzhou troops serve the same lord—will they play bandit among their own?

sentences.zh: ”乃讨之，数之以罪。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he attacked them and enumerated their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: " He attacked them and denounced their crimes.

sentences.zh: 青州兵遽走诣太祖自诉。

translations.literal: The Qingzhou troops hastily ran to the Grand Progenitor to complain on their own behalf.
translations.idiomatic: The Qingzhou troops raced ahead to Cao Cao to lodge their complaint.

sentences.zh: 禁既至，先立营垒，不时谒太祖。

translations.literal: When Jin arrived, first he established camp fortifications and did not promptly pay visit to the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Jin arrived he threw up entrenchments first instead of hurrying in to see Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 或谓禁：“青州兵已诉君矣，宜促诣公辨之。

translations.literal: Someone said to Jin: "The Qingzhou troops have already complained against you; you ought hastily to go to the lord to argue it.
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged him, "The Qingzhou men have already denounced you—you should go to the duke at once and clear yourself.

sentences.zh: ”禁曰：“今贼在后，追至无时，不先为备，何以待敌？

translations.literal: " Jin said: "Now the bandits are behind us; pursuit may arrive at any time—if we do not first make preparations, by what means shall we await the enemy?
translations.idiomatic: " Yu Jin replied, "The enemy is still on our heels and could strike at any moment. Without a secure camp how can we face them?

sentences.zh: 且公聪明，谮诉何缘！

translations.literal: Moreover the lord is intelligent and perspicacious—what basis for slanderous complaint!
translations.idiomatic: Besides, our lord is too astute to be swayed by malicious tales!

sentences.zh: ”徐凿堑安营讫，乃入谒，具陈其状。

translations.literal: " Slowly he dug moats and finished settling the camp, then entered to pay visit and fully stated the situation.
translations.idiomatic: " Only after he had dug ditches and completed his camp did he go in to report the whole affair.

sentences.zh: 太祖悦，谓禁曰：“淯水之难，吾其急也，将军在乱能整，讨暴坚垒，有不可动之节，虽古名将，何以加之！

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor was pleased and said to Jin: "At the disaster of the Yu water I was in extremity; the general in disorder was able to set things in order, attacked violence and made firm ramparts, had integrity that could not be moved—even ancient famous generals, how could one add beyond that!
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao was pleased and told him, "At the Yu River I was in desperate straits; you kept order in chaos, punished marauders, and threw up a defensible camp—such steadfastness would honor any general in history.

sentences.zh: ”於是录禁前后功，封益寿亭侯。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he recorded Jin's former and later merit and enfeoffed him as marquis of the Yishou village.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon registered Yu Jin's cumulative service and enfeoffed him as marquis of Yishou village.

sentences.zh: 复从攻张绣於穰，禽吕布於下邳，别与史涣、曹仁攻眭固於射犬，破斩之。

translations.literal: Again he followed in attacking Zhang Xiu at Rang, captured Lü Bu at Xiapi, separately together with Shi Huan and Cao Ren attacked Sui Gu at Shequan, defeated and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: He again served against Zhang Xiu at Rang, helped capture Lü Bu at Xiapi, and with Shi Huan and Cao Ren stormed Shequan, where he killed Sui Gu.

sentences.zh: 太祖初征袁绍，绍兵盛，禁原为先登。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor first campaigned against Yuan Shao, Shao's troops were abundant, and Jin volunteered to be first to ascend.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Yuan Shao campaign, when Shao's army was strongest, Yu Jin volunteered for the assault echelon.

sentences.zh: 太祖壮之，乃遣步卒二千人，使禁将，守延津以拒绍，太祖引军还官渡。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor thought him brave and thereupon dispatched two thousand foot soldiers, ordered Jin to lead them, guard Yanjin to resist Shao, and the Grand Progenitor led the army back to Guandu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao approved and gave him two thousand foot to hold Yanjin against Yuan Shao while the main body drew back to Guandu.

sentences.zh: 刘备以徐州叛，太祖东征之。

translations.literal: Liu Bei rebelled with Xu Province; the Grand Progenitor campaigned east against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei seized Xu Province in revolt, Cao Cao marched east against him.

sentences.zh: 绍攻禁，禁坚守，绍不能拔。

translations.literal: Shao attacked Jin; Jin firmly defended; Shao could not take him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao attacked Yu Jin's position but could not break his defense.

sentences.zh: 复与乐进等将步骑五千，击绍别营，从延津西南缘河至汲、获嘉二县，焚烧保聚三十餘屯，斩首获生各数千，降绍将何茂、王摩等二十餘人。

translations.literal: Again together with Yue Jin and others he led five thousand foot and horse, struck Shao's separate camp, from southwest of Yanjin along the river reached the two counties of Ji and Huojia, burned more than thirty fortified gatherings, beheaded and captured alive each several thousand, and caused to surrender Shao's generals He Mao, Wang Mo, and more than twenty others.
translations.idiomatic: With Yue Jin he took five thousand mixed troops against Yuan Shao's detached camps, followed the river southwest from Yanjin through Ji and Huojia, burned over thirty fortified hamlets, took thousands of heads and prisoners, and brought more than twenty of Shao's officers including He Mao and Wang Mo to surrender.

sentences.zh: 太祖复使禁别将屯原武，击绍别营於杜氏津，破之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor again ordered Jin separately to lead and garrison Yuanwu, attacked Shao's separate camp at Du's Ford, and defeated it.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao also sent him to garrison Yuanwu and destroy a Yuan Shao outpost at Du's Ford.

sentences.zh: 迁裨将军，后从还官渡。

translations.literal: He was promoted to major general; afterward he followed in returning to Guandu.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to major general and rejoined the main army at Guandu.

sentences.zh: 太祖与绍连营，起土山相对。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor and Shao linked camps and raised earthen mounds facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao and Yuan Shao faced each other in linked camps with opposing siege mounds.

sentences.zh: 绍射营中，士卒多死伤，军中惧。

translations.literal: Shao shot into the camp; soldiers many died and were wounded; in the army there was fear.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao's archers raked the camp, inflicting heavy casualties and spreading panic.

sentences.zh: 禁督守土山，力战，气益奋。

translations.literal: Jin supervised defense of the earthen mound, fought hard, and his spirit grew more aroused.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin directed the defense of the mound and fought so fiercely that his men's morale rose.

sentences.zh: 绍破，迁偏将军。

translations.literal: When Shao was broken, he was promoted to lieutenant general.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Shao's defeat he became lieutenant general.

sentences.zh: 冀州平。

translations.literal: Ji Province was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Province was pacified.

sentences.zh: 昌豨复叛，遣禁征之。

translations.literal: Chang Xi again rebelled; he dispatched Jin to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang Xi rebelled again, Cao Cao sent Yu Jin against him.

sentences.zh: 禁急进攻豨；

translations.literal: Jin urgently advanced and attacked Xi;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin pressed the attack hard;

sentences.zh: 豨与禁有旧，诣禁降。

translations.literal: Xi with Jin had old ties; he went to Jin to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Xi, an old acquaintance, came to Yu Jin's camp to yield.

sentences.zh: 诸将皆以为豨已降，当送诣太祖，禁曰：“诸君不知公常令乎！

translations.literal: The various generals all thought Xi had already surrendered and ought to be sent to the Grand Progenitor; Jin said: "Gentlemen, do you not know the lord's standing order!
translations.idiomatic: The other generals wanted to send Chang Xi to Cao Cao, but Yu Jin said, "Have you forgotten the standing order?

sentences.zh: 围而后降者不赦。

translations.literal: Those who after being surrounded then surrender are not pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Those who surrender only after we have them surrounded are not spared.

sentences.zh: 夫奉法行令，事上之节也。

translations.literal: Now upholding law and carrying out orders is the integrity of serving a superior.
translations.idiomatic: To enforce the law and obey orders is how a subordinate serves his lord.

sentences.zh: 豨虽旧友，禁可失节乎！

translations.literal: Although Xi is an old friend, can Jin lose integrity!
translations.idiomatic: Chang Xi may be an old friend, but am I to break discipline for his sake?

sentences.zh: ”自临与豨决，陨涕而斩之。

translations.literal: " He personally came to execute Xi with Xi, shed tears, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: " He went in person to say farewell, wept, and had Chang Xi executed.

sentences.zh: 是时太祖军淳于，闻而叹曰：“豨降不诣吾而归禁，岂非命耶！

translations.literal: At that time the Grand Progenitor's army was at Chunyu; hearing it he sighed and said: "Xi surrendered but did not come to me and instead went to Jin—is it not fate!
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao was at Chunyu when he heard the news and sighed, "Chang Xi surrendered to Yu Jin instead of to me—was that not his fate?

sentences.zh: ”益重禁。

translations.literal: " He all the more esteemed Jin.
translations.idiomatic: " He respected Yu Jin all the more for it.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之以为围而后降，法虽不赦；

translations.literal: 〈Your servant Songzhi considers: though those who after being surrounded then surrender, by law are not pardoned;
translations.idiomatic: 〈Pei Songzhi observes that although the law does not pardon those who yield only after encirclement;

sentences.zh: 囚而送之，未为违命。

translations.literal: to imprison and send them is not reckoned disobeying orders.
translations.idiomatic: to take him prisoner and send him in chains would not have violated orders.

sentences.zh: 禁曾不为旧交希冀万一，而肆其好杀之心，以戾众人之议，所以卒为降虏，死加恶谥，宜哉。〉

translations.literal: Jin never for old friendship hoped for the one-in-ten-thousand, but unleashed his fondness for killing, thereby going against the multitude's discussion; therefore in the end he became a surrendered captive, and in death had an evil posthumous title—fitting indeed.〉
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin never showed his old friend the slightest mercy but indulged his appetite for killing and defied common opinion—small wonder he ended a prisoner of war and earned a shameful posthumous name.〉

sentences.zh: 东海平，拜禁虎威将军。

translations.literal: When Donghai was pacified, Jin was appointed general of tiger might.
translations.idiomatic: After Donghai was pacified he was named general of tiger might.

sentences.zh: 后与臧霸等攻梅成，张辽、张郃等讨陈兰。

translations.literal: Afterward together with Zang Ba and others he attacked Mei Cheng, while Zhang Liao, Zhang He, and others campaigned against Chen Lan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined Zang Ba against Mei Cheng while Zhang Liao and Zhang He dealt with Chen Lan.

sentences.zh: 禁到，成举众三千餘人降。

translations.literal: When Jin arrived, Cheng raised his multitude of more than three thousand men and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Jin arrived, Mei Cheng brought more than three thousand men to surrender.

sentences.zh: 既降复叛，其众奔兰。

translations.literal: Having surrendered he again rebelled; his multitude fled to Lan.
translations.idiomatic: He surrendered, then rebelled again, and his followers fled to Chen Lan.

sentences.zh: 辽等与兰相持，军食少，禁运粮前后相属，辽遂斩兰、成。

translations.literal: Liao and others locked horns with Lan; army food was scant; Jin transported grain, front and rear linked in succession, and Liao thereupon beheaded Lan and Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liao's force was locked with Chen Lan and short of supplies; Yu Jin kept grain convoys moving until Zhang Liao could behead both Chen Lan and Mei Cheng.

sentences.zh: 增邑二百户，并前千二百户。

translations.literal: His fief was increased by two hundred households; together with the previous it was one thousand two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred more households were added to his fief, for twelve hundred in all.

sentences.zh: 是时，禁与张辽、乐进、张郃、徐晃俱为名将，太祖每征伐，咸递行为军锋，还为后拒；

translations.literal: At this time Jin together with Zhang Liao, Yue Jin, Zhang He, and Xu Huang were all famous generals; whenever the Grand Progenitor campaigned, all in turn acted as army vanguard, and returning acted as rear guard;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin, Zhang Liao, Yue Jin, Zhang He, and Xu Huang were counted among the finest commanders of the day; on each expedition they took turns leading the van or covering the retreat;

sentences.zh: 而禁持军严整，得贼财物，无所私入，由是赏赐特重。

translations.literal: but Jin held the army strict and orderly; captured enemy goods and wealth, nothing privately entered his own; by this his rewards and gifts were especially heavy.
translations.idiomatic: but Yu Jin ran the tightest ship and never pocketed booty, for which he received unusually rich rewards.

sentences.zh: 然以法御下，不甚得士众心。

translations.literal: Yet by law he controlled those below and did not greatly win the hearts of officers and troops.
translations.idiomatic: His strict legalism won him little affection from the ranks.

sentences.zh: 太祖常恨硃灵，欲夺其营。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor constantly resented Zhu Ling and wished to seize his camp.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao had long resented Zhu Ling and wished to strip him of his command.

sentences.zh: 以禁有威重，遣禁将数十骑，赍令书，径诣灵营夺其军，灵及其部众莫敢动；

translations.literal: Because Jin had awe-inspiring weight, he dispatched Jin leading several tens of horsemen, carrying written orders, going straight to Ling's camp to seize his army, and Ling together with his troops and multitude none dared move;
translations.idiomatic: Because Yu Jin commanded respect, Cao Cao sent him with a few dozen horsemen and written orders straight into Zhu Ling's camp to take over the troops; Zhu Ling and his men dared not resist;

sentences.zh: 乃以灵为禁部下督，众皆震服，其见惮如此。

translations.literal: thereupon he made Ling a supervisor under Jin's command; the multitude all were awed and submitted—thus he was feared.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ling was made a subordinate under Yu Jin, and the army stood in awe of the latter's authority.

sentences.zh: 迁左将军，假节钺，分邑五百户，封一子列侯。

translations.literal: He was promoted to general of the left, lent the battle-axe insignia, five hundred households of fief were divided off, and one son was enfeoffed as full marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to general of the left with axe-and-baton authority, received another five hundred households, and a son was enfeoffed as a full marquis.

sentences.zh: 张郃字雋乂，河间鄚人也。

translations.literal: Zhang He, courtesy name Junyi, was a man of Mo in Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang He, courtesy name Junyi, came from Mo county in Hejian.

sentences.zh: 汉末应募讨黄巾，为军司马，属韩馥。

translations.literal: At the end of Han he answered recruitment to campaign against the Yellow Turbans, became major of the army, and was subordinate to Han Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Han he enlisted against the Yellow Turbans, became an army major under Han Fu.

sentences.zh: 馥败，以兵归袁绍。

translations.literal: When Fu was defeated, he attached his troops to Yuan Shao.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Fu fell he brought his troops over to Yuan Shao.

sentences.zh: 绍以郃为校尉，使拒公孙瓚。

translations.literal: Shao appointed He colonel and ordered him to resist Gongsun Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao made him a colonel and sent him against Gongsun Zan.

sentences.zh: 瓚破，郃功多，迁宁国中郎将。

translations.literal: When Zan was broken, He had much merit and was promoted to General of the Gentlemen of the Household Who Pacifies the State.
translations.idiomatic: After Gongsun Zan's defeat his services earned him promotion to general of the household who pacifies the state.

sentences.zh: 太祖与袁绍相拒於官渡，

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor and Yuan Shao faced each other at Guandu,
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao and Yuan Shao confronted each other at Guandu,

sentences.zh: 〈《汉晋春秋曰：郃说绍曰：“公虽连胜，然勿与曹公战也，密遣轻骑钞绝其南，则兵自败矣。

translations.literal: 〈The Han Jin chunqiu says: He urged Shao, saying: "Although you lord have repeatedly won, yet do not fight Lord Cao; secretly dispatch light cavalry to raid and cut off his south, then the troops will defeat themselves.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Han Jin chunqiu records Zhang He urging Yuan Shao: "Even after your victories, do not meet Cao Cao in pitched battle; send light cavalry secretly to raid his southern lines and his army will collapse of itself.

sentences.zh: ”绍不从之。〉

translations.literal: " Shao did not follow it.〉
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan Shao refused to listen.〉

sentences.zh: 绍遣将淳于琼等督运屯乌巢，太祖自将急击之。

translations.literal: Shao dispatched generals Chunyu Qiong and others to supervise transport and garrison Wuchao; the Grand Progenitor personally led a rapid strike against them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao posted Chunyu Qiong and others to guard the supply depot at Wuchao, and Cao Cao led a lightning strike against them in person.

sentences.zh: 郃说绍曰：“曹公兵精，往必破琼等；

translations.literal: He urged Shao, saying: "Lord Cao's troops are picked; if he goes he is sure to break Qiong and the others;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang He warned Yuan Shao, "Cao Cao's troops are elite; if he goes he will crush Chunyu Qiong;

sentences.zh: 琼等破，则将军事去矣，宜急引兵救之。

translations.literal: when Qiong and the others are broken, then the general's affair will be lost; it is fitting urgently to lead troops to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: once that depot falls your cause is lost—you must march relief to Wuchao at once.

sentences.zh: ”郭图曰：“郃计非也。

translations.literal: " Guo Tu said: "Zhang He's plan is not right.
translations.idiomatic: " Guo Tu said, "Zhang He's strategy is wrong.

sentences.zh: 不如攻其本营，势必还，此为不救而自解也。

translations.literal: It is better to attack his main camp; the situation will force him to return—this is not rescuing yet resolving of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Better to strike his main camp; he will be forced to pull back—that ends the crisis without a relief column.

sentences.zh: ”郃曰：“曹公营固，攻之必不拔，若琼等见禽，吾属尽为虏矣。

translations.literal: " He said: "Lord Cao's camp is solid; attacking it is sure not to be taken; if Qiong and the others are captured, we sorts will all become captives.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang He replied, "Cao Cao's fortifications will not fall to a hasty assault; if Chunyu Qiong is taken we are all prisoners.

sentences.zh: ”绍但遣轻骑救琼，而以重兵攻太祖营，不能下。

translations.literal: " Shao only dispatched light cavalry to rescue Qiong, but with heavy troops attacked the Grand Progenitor's camp and could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan Shao sent only light horse to relieve Wuchao while his main force hammered Cao Cao's camp without success.

sentences.zh: 太祖果破琼等，绍军溃。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor indeed broke Qiong and the others, and Shao's army collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao destroyed Chunyu Qiong as predicted, and Yuan Shao's army collapsed.

sentences.zh: 图惭，又更谮郃曰：“郃快军败，出言不逊。

translations.literal: Tu was ashamed and again slandered He, saying: "He rejoices in the army's defeat and his words are not deferential.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, Guo Tu slandered Zhang He, claiming he had gloated over the defeat and spoken disrespectfully.

sentences.zh: ”郃惧，乃归太祖。

translations.literal: " He feared and thereupon submitted to the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: " Fearing Guo Tu's malice, Zhang He went over to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案《武纪》及《袁绍传》并云袁绍使张郃、高览攻太祖营，郃等闻淳于琼破，遂来降，绍众於是大溃。

translations.literal: 〈Your servant Songzhi examines: the Wu ji and the Yuan Shao zhuan alike say Yuan Shao ordered Zhang He and Gao Lan to attack the Grand Progenitor's camp; He and others hearing that Chunyu Qiong was broken thereupon came to surrender, and Shao's multitude thereupon greatly collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Pei Songzhi notes that the Wu ji and Yuan Shao's biography both say Yuan Shao ordered Zhang He and Gao Lan to assault Cao Cao's camp, that they surrendered when they heard Chunyu Qiong had fallen, and that Yuan Shao's host then disintegrated.

sentences.zh: 是则缘郃等降而后绍军坏也。

translations.literal: This then is because He and others surrendered and afterward Shao's army was ruined.
translations.idiomatic: That version makes the collapse of Yuan Shao's army a consequence of Zhang He's defection.

sentences.zh: 至如此传，为绍军先溃，惧郭图之谮，然后归太祖，为参错不同矣。〉

translations.literal: As for like this biography, it makes Shao's army first collapse, fearing Guo Tu's slander, then submit to the Grand Progenitor—it is contradictory and not the same.〉
translations.idiomatic: This biography, by contrast, has the army rout first and Zhang He defect to Cao Cao for fear of Guo Tu—the two accounts do not agree.〉

sentences.zh: 太祖得郃甚喜，谓曰：“昔子胥不早寤，自使身危，岂若微子去殷、韩信归汉邪？

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor obtaining He was very pleased and said to him: "In the past Zixu did not awaken early and himself caused his body to be imperiled—how could that compare to Weizi leaving Yin or Han Xin returning to Han?
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao was delighted to gain Zhang He and told him, "Wu Zixu woke too late and perished for it; would you not rather be like Weizi leaving the Shang or Han Xin coming over to the Han?

sentences.zh: ”拜郃偏将军，封都亭侯。

translations.literal: " He appointed He lieutenant general and enfeoffed him as marquis of the metropolitan village.
translations.idiomatic: " He named Zhang He lieutenant general and enfeoffed him as marquis of a village at the capital.

sentences.zh: 授以众，从攻鄴，拔之。

translations.literal: He entrusted him with troops; he followed in attacking Ye and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao gave him a command, and he took part in the storming of Ye.

sentences.zh: 又从击袁谭於渤海，别将军围雍奴，大破之。

translations.literal: Again he followed in striking Yuan Tan at Bohai; as a separate general he besieged Yongnu and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Yuan Tan in Bohai, then led a separate column to invest Yongnu and shattered the defenders.

sentences.zh: 从讨柳城，与张辽俱为军锋，以功迁平狄将军。

translations.literal: He followed in campaigning against Liucheng; together with Zhang Liao both were army vanguard; by merit he was promoted to general who pacifies the Di.
translations.idiomatic: On the Liucheng expedition he and Zhang Liao spearheaded the army and he was promoted to general who pacifies the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 别征东莱，讨管承，又与张辽讨陈兰、梅成等，破之。

translations.literal: Separately he campaigned in Donglai, attacked Guan Cheng, and again together with Zhang He campaigned against Chen Lan, Mei Cheng, and others, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned separately in Donglai against Guan Cheng and joined Zhang Liao in defeating Chen Lan and Mei Cheng.

sentences.zh: 从破马超、韩遂於渭南。

translations.literal: He followed in defeating Ma Chao and Han Sui south of the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in breaking Ma Chao and Han Sui on the south bank of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 围安定，降杨秋。

translations.literal: They besieged Anding and caused Yang Qiu to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: They besieged Anding until Yang Qiu submitted.

sentences.zh: 与夏侯渊讨鄜贼梁兴及武都氐。

translations.literal: Together with Xiahou Yuan he campaigned against the Fu bandit Liang Xing and the Di of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: With Xiahou Yuan he campaigned against the Fu bandit Liang Xing and the Wudu Di.

sentences.zh: 又破马超，平宋建。

translations.literal: Again he defeated Ma Chao and pacified Song Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Ma Chao again and put down Song Jian.

sentences.zh: 太祖征张鲁，先遣郃督诸军讨兴和氐王窦茂。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor campaigned against Zhang Lu, first he dispatched He to supervise the various armies in campaigning against the Xinghe Di king Dou Mao.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhang Lu campaign Cao Cao first sent Zhang He to lead the forces against the Di king Dou Mao at Xinghe.

sentences.zh: 太祖从散关入汉中，又先遣郃督步卒五千於前通路。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor entered Hanzhong from Sanguan Pass, and again first dispatched He to supervise five thousand foot soldiers in front to open the road.
translations.idiomatic: As Cao Cao entered Hanzhong from Sanguan, he again sent Zhang He ahead with five thousand foot to clear the route.

sentences.zh: 至阳平，鲁降，太祖还，留郃与夏侯渊等守汉中，拒刘备。

translations.literal: Reaching Yangping, Lu surrendered; the Grand Progenitor returned, left He together with Xiahou Yuan and others to guard Hanzhong, and resist Liu Bei.
translations.idiomatic: At Yangping, Zhang Lu surrendered; Cao Cao withdrew but left Zhang He with Xiahou Yuan to hold Hanzhong against Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 郃别督诸军，降巴东、巴西二郡，徙其民於汉中。

translations.literal: He separately supervised the various armies, caused the two commanderies of Badong and Baxi to surrender, and moved their people to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang He commanded a separate force that brought Badong and Baxi to terms and resettled their people in Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 进军宕渠，为备将张飞所拒，引还南郑。

translations.literal: Advancing the army to Dangqu, he was resisted by Bei's general Zhang Fei and led the army back to Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced on Dangqu but was blocked by Liu Bei's general Zhang Fei and fell back to Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 拜荡寇将军。

translations.literal: He was appointed general who sweeps away bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He was named general who sweeps away bandits.

sentences.zh: 刘备屯阳平，郃屯广石。

translations.literal: Liu Bei garrisoned Yangping; He garrisoned Guangshi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei held Yangping while Zhang He held Guangshi.

sentences.zh: 备以精卒万餘，分为十部，夜急攻郃。

translations.literal: Bei with picked troops of more than ten thousand, divided into ten divisions, by night urgently attacked He.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei threw more than ten thousand elite troops in ten columns against Zhang He in a night assault.

sentences.zh: 郃率亲兵搏战，备不能克。

translations.literal: He led personal troops in close combat; Bei could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang He led his bodyguard in a stand-up fight and Liu Bei could not break him.

sentences.zh: 其后备於走马谷烧都围，渊救火，从他道与备相遇，交战，短兵接刃。

translations.literal: Afterward Bei at Zouma Valley burned the capital stockade; Yuan went to fight the fire, from another road encountered Bei, joined battle, and short weapons met blades.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liu Bei fired the stockade at Zouma Valley; Xiahou Yuan rode out to fight the blaze, met Liu Bei by another route, and the two forces clashed hand-to-hand.

sentences.zh: 渊遂没，郃还阳平。

translations.literal: Yuan thereupon perished; He returned to Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Yuan fell in the fighting, and Zhang He withdrew to Yangping.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略曰：渊虽为都督，刘备惮郃而易渊。

translations.literal: 〈The Wei lüe says: Although Yuan was commander-in-chief, Liu Bei feared He and thought lightly of Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wei lüe notes that although Xiahou Yuan held supreme command, Liu Bei feared Zhang He more than he did Xiahou Yuan.

sentences.zh: 及杀渊，备曰：“当得其魁，用此何为邪！

translations.literal: When Yuan was killed, Bei said: "We ought to have caught their chief—what use was this!
translations.idiomatic: When Xiahou Yuan died, Liu Bei said, "We should have taken their real leader—what good was killing him?

sentences.zh: 当是时，新失元帅，恐为备所乘，三军皆失色。

translations.literal: At that time, having newly lost the commander-in-chief, they feared being exploited by Bei; the three armies all lost color.
translations.idiomatic: With their commander just slain and Liu Bei ready to exploit the gap, the whole army went pale with dread.

sentences.zh: 渊司马郭淮乃令众曰：“张将军，国家名将，刘备所惮；

translations.literal: Yuan's major Guo Huai thereupon ordered the multitude, saying: "General Zhang is a famous general of the state whom Liu Bei fears;
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Yuan's chief of staff Guo Huai told the troops, "General Zhang is one of the empire's foremost commanders and the man Liu Bei dreads;

sentences.zh: 今日事急，非张将军不能安也。

translations.literal: Today's affair is urgent; unless it is General Zhang, none can settle it.
translations.idiomatic: in this crisis only General Zhang can steady us.

sentences.zh: ”遂推郃为军主。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they pushed He to be army master.
translations.idiomatic: " They thereupon acclaimed Zhang He as commander.

sentences.zh: 郃出，勒兵安陈，诸将皆受郃节度，众心乃定。

translations.literal: He came out, restrained the troops and settled the formation; the various generals all received He's command and control; the hearts of the multitude were then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang He took command, drew up the battle line, brought every general under his orders, and restored the army's confidence.

sentences.zh: 太祖在长安，遣使假郃节。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor was at Chang'an and dispatched an envoy to lend He the credential insignia.
translations.idiomatic: From Chang'an Cao Cao sent an envoy to invest Zhang He with the baton of authority.

sentences.zh: 太祖遂自至汉中，刘备保高山不敢战。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor thereupon personally came to Hanzhong; Liu Bei protected the high mountains and did not dare fight.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao then came to Hanzhong in person, while Liu Bei held the heights and refused battle.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃引出汉中诸军，郃还屯陈仓。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor thereupon led out the various armies of Hanzhong, and He returned to garrison at Chencang.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao then withdrew the Hanzhong armies and posted Zhang He at Chencang.

sentences.zh: 郃识变数，善处营陈，料战势地形，无不如计，自诸葛亮皆惮之。

translations.literal: He understood the changes of circumstance, was good at disposing camps and formations, assessed battle situation and terrain, and nothing failed to match his plans—even Zhuge Liang all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang He read the shifting odds, handled encampments and deployments with skill, and judged terrain and battle flow so shrewdly that his plans never failed—even Zhuge Liang respected him.

sentences.zh: 郃虽武将而爱乐儒士，尝荐同乡卑湛经明行修，诏曰：“昔祭遵为将，奏置五经大夫，居军中，与诸生雅歌投壶。

translations.literal: Although He was a military officer, he loved and delighted in Confucian scholars; once he recommended his fellow townsman Bei Zhan, who was clear in the classics and cultivated in conduct; an edict said: "In the past Ji Zun as general memorialized to establish doctors of the Five Classics, dwelt in the army, and with the various students sang refined songs and played pitch-pot.
translations.idiomatic: Though a soldier, Zhang He delighted in scholars; he once recommended his townsman Bei Zhan for classical learning and upright conduct, and an edict replied, "When Ji Zun was a general he had doctors of the Five Classics in camp who sang and played pitch-pot with the students.

sentences.zh: 今将军外勒戎旅，内存国朝。

translations.literal: Now the general outwardly restrains the martial brigades, inwardly cherishes the court of the state.
translations.idiomatic: You lead armies in the field yet hold the court in your heart.

sentences.zh: 朕嘉将军之意，今擢湛为博士。

translations.literal: We approve the general's intent; now We promote Zhan to erudite.
translations.idiomatic: We commend your intent and hereby promote Bei Zhan to erudite.

sentences.zh: 诸葛亮复出祁山，诏郃督诸将西至略阳，亮还保祁山，郃追至木门，与亮军交战，飞矢中郃右膝，薨，

translations.literal: When Zhuge Liang again came out to Qishan, an edict ordered He to supervise the various generals west to Lueyang; Liang returned to protect Qishan; He pursued to Mumen, joined battle with Liang's army, a flying arrow struck He's right knee, and he died,
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Liang again drove toward Qishan, an edict sent Zhang He west to Lueyang; as Zhuge Liang fell back on Qishan, Zhang He pursued to Mumen, where in the fighting an arrow struck his right knee and he died,

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：亮军退，司马宣王使郃追之，郃曰：“军法，围城必开出路，归军勿追。

translations.literal: 〈The Wei lüe says: When Liang's army withdrew, Sima Xuanwang ordered He to pursue them; He said: "By military law, when besieging a city one must open an escape route; do not pursue a withdrawing army.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wei lüe records that when Zhuge Liang withdrew, Sima Yi ordered Zhang He to pursue; Zhang He said, "The art of war says to leave a way out of a siege and never to chase a retreating host.

sentences.zh: ”宣王不听。

translations.literal: " Xuanwang did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " Sima Yi would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 郃不得已，遂进。

translations.literal: He had no choice and thereupon advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang He had no choice but to advance.

sentences.zh: 蜀军乘高布伏，弓弩乱发，矢中郃髀。〉

translations.literal: The Shu army rode the heights and laid ambush; crossbows shot wildly; an arrow struck He's thigh.〉
translations.idiomatic: The Shu troops held the heights in ambush and raked him with bolts; an arrow struck him in the thigh.〉

sentences.zh: 谥曰壮侯。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Marquis Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Marquis Zhuang, "the Stalwart."

sentences.zh: 子雄嗣。

translations.literal: The son Xiong inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhang Xiong inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 郃前后征伐有功，明帝分郃户，封郃四子列侯。

translations.literal: He before and after campaigning had merit; Emperor Ming divided He's households and enfeoffed He's four sons as full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: For his long record of service Emperor Ming divided his fief and enfeoffed four of Zhang He's sons as full marquises.

sentences.zh: 赐小子爵关内侯。

translations.literal: His youngest son was granted the noble rank of secondary marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son received a secondary marquisate at court.

sentences.zh: 徐晃字公明，河东杨人也。

translations.literal: Xu Huang, courtesy name Gongming, was a man of Yang in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huang, courtesy name Gongming, came from Yang in Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 为郡吏，从车骑将军杨奉讨贼有功，拜骑都尉。

translations.literal: He was a commandery clerk; following General of Chariots and Cavalry Yang Feng in campaigning against bandits he had merit and was appointed colonel of cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: A commandery clerk, he followed the general of chariots and cavalry Yang Feng against bandits, distinguished himself, and was named colonel of cavalry.

sentences.zh: 李傕、郭汜之乱长安也，晃说奉，令与天子还洛阳，奉从其计。

translations.literal: When Li Jue and Guo Si threw Chang'an into turmoil, Huang persuaded Feng to cause him together with the Son of Heaven to return to Luoyang, and Feng followed his plan.
translations.idiomatic: During Li Jue and Guo Si's rampage in Chang'an, Xu Huang persuaded Yang Feng to escort the emperor back to Luoyang, and Yang Feng agreed.

sentences.zh: 天子渡河至安邑，封晃都亭侯。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven crossed the Yellow River and reached Anyi; he enfeoffed Huang as marquis of the metropolitan village.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor crossed the river to Anyi, Xu Huang was enfeoffed as marquis of a village at the capital.

sentences.zh: 及到洛阳，韩暹、董承日争斗，晃说奉令归太祖；

translations.literal: When they reached Luoyang, Han Xian and Dong Cheng daily quarreled and fought; Huang persuaded Feng to order submission to the Grand Progenitor;
translations.idiomatic: At Luoyang, where Han Xian and Dong Cheng quarreled daily, Xu Huang urged Yang Feng to submit to Cao Cao;

sentences.zh: 奉欲从之，后悔。

translations.literal: Feng wished to follow it, afterward regretted.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Feng meant to agree, then thought better of it.

sentences.zh: 太祖讨奉於梁，晃遂归太祖。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor campaigned against Feng at Liang; Huang thereupon submitted to the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao attacked Yang Feng at Liang, Xu Huang went over to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 太祖授晃兵，使击卷、

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor entrusted Huang with troops and ordered him to strike Juan and
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao gave Xu Huang troops and ordered him to attack the bandits at Juan (see following gloss) and

sentences.zh: 〈卷音墟权反。〉

translations.literal: 〈Editorial gloss: the place-name character here is glossed with a fanqie spelling (initial qu-, final -uan).〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Editorial note: the character in the place name is read by the fanqie formula given in the Chinese margin.〉

sentences.zh: 原武贼，破之，拜裨将军。

translations.literal: the Yuanwu bandits; he defeated them and was appointed major general.
translations.idiomatic: those at Yuanwu; he crushed them and was promoted to major general.

sentences.zh: 从征吕布，别降布将赵庶、李邹等。

translations.literal: He followed in campaigning against Lü Bu; separately he caused Bu's generals Zhao Shu, Li Zou, and others to surrender.
