translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Lü Bu and separately induced generals such as Zhao Shu and Li Zou to surrender.

sentences.zh: 与史涣斩眭固於河内。

translations.literal: Together with Shi Huan he beheaded Sui Gu in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: With Shi Huan he executed Sui Gu in Henei.

sentences.zh: 从破刘备，又从破颜良，拔白马，进至延津，破文丑，拜偏将军。

translations.literal: He followed in defeating Liu Bei, again followed in defeating Yan Liang, took Baima, advanced to Yanjin, defeated Wen Chou, and was appointed lieutenant general.
translations.idiomatic: He helped defeat Liu Bei, then Yan Liang, took Baima, advanced to Yanjin, killed Wen Chou, and was made lieutenant general.

sentences.zh: 与曹洪击氵隐强贼祝臂，破之，又与史涣击袁绍运车於故市，功最多，封都亭侯。

translations.literal: Together with Cao Hong he struck the Yinqiang bandit Zhu Bi, defeated him, and again together with Shi Huan struck Yuan Shao's transport carts at Gushi; his merit was the greatest, and he was enfeoffed as marquis of the metropolitan village.
translations.idiomatic: With Cao Hong he crushed the bandit Zhu Bi from the Yinqiang district in Runan, then with Shi Huan burned Yuan Shao's supply train at Gushi, a feat that won him the greatest credit and a village marquisate at the capital.

sentences.zh: 太祖既围鄴，破邯郸，易阳令韩范伪以城降而拒守，太祖遣晃攻之。

translations.literal: After the Grand Progenitor had besieged Ye and broken Handan, the Yiyang magistrate Han Fan falsely offered to surrender the city but refused to defend; the Grand Progenitor dispatched Huang to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: After Ye was besieged and Handan taken, the magistrate Han Fan of Yiyang feigned surrender then shut the gates; Cao Cao sent Xu Huang against him.

sentences.zh: 晃至，飞矢城中，为陈成败。

translations.literal: When Huang arrived, he shot arrows into the city and for them explained success and defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huang shot letters into the town explaining the consequences of resistance or submission.

sentences.zh: 范悔，晃辄降之。

translations.literal: Fan repented; Huang thereupon caused him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fan reconsidered and Xu Huang accepted his surrender.

sentences.zh: 既而言於太祖曰：“二袁未破，诸城未下者倾耳而听，今日灭易阳，明日皆以死守，恐河北无定时也。

translations.literal: Afterward he spoke to the Grand Progenitor, saying: "The two Yuans are not yet broken; the various cities not yet taken all incline their ears and listen; if today we extinguish Yiyang, tomorrow all will defend to the death; I fear Hebei will have no time of peace.
translations.idiomatic: He then told Cao Cao, "The two Yuans still stand, and every city still holding out is listening; if you wipe out Yiyang now, the rest will fight to the last man and the north may never be settled.

sentences.zh: 原公降易阳以示诸城，则莫不望风。

translations.literal: I beg the lord to accept Yiyang's surrender to show the various cities, then none will fail to submit at the wind's direction.
translations.idiomatic: Accept this surrender as an example and the other towns will yield without a fight.

sentences.zh: ”太祖善之。

translations.literal: " The Grand Progenitor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao approved the advice.

sentences.zh: 别讨毛城，设伏兵掩击，破三屯。

translations.literal: Separately he campaigned against Maocheng, set ambush troops for a surprise strike, and broke three encampments.
translations.idiomatic: On a separate mission against Maocheng he ambushed and overran three enemy camps.

sentences.zh: 从破袁谭於南皮，讨平原叛贼，克之。

translations.literal: He followed in defeating Yuan Tan at Nanpi, campaigned against the Pingyuan rebel bandits, and overcame them.
translations.idiomatic: He helped defeat Yuan Tan at Nanpi and crushed the rebels in Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 从征蹋顿，拜横野将军。

translations.literal: He followed in campaigning against Tadun and was appointed general who sweeps the wilderness.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Tadun and was named general who sweeps the wilderness.

sentences.zh: 从征荆州，别屯樊，讨中庐、临沮、宜城贼。

translations.literal: He followed in campaigning against Jing Province; separately he garrisoned Fan and campaigned against the bandits of Zhonglu, Linju, and Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Jingzhou expedition, held Fan on a detached posting, and campaigned against bandits in Zhonglu, Linju, and Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 又与满宠讨关羽於汉津，与曹仁击周瑜於江陵。

translations.literal: Again together with Man Chong he campaigned against Guan Yu at Han Ford; together with Cao Ren he struck Zhou Yu at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: With Man Chong he fought Guan Yu at Han Ford, and with Cao Ren he fought Zhou Yu at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 十五年，讨太原反者，围大陵，拔之，斩贼帅商曜。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he campaigned against the rebels of Taiyuan, besieged Daling, took it, and beheaded the bandit chief Shang Yao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he put down the Taiyuan revolt, stormed Daling, and executed the rebel leader Shang Yao.

sentences.zh: 韩遂、马超等反关右，遣晃屯汾阴以抚河东，赐牛酒，令上先人墓。

translations.literal: When Han Sui, Ma Chao, and others rebelled west of the pass, he dispatched Huang to garrison Fenyin to pacify Hedong, bestowed oxen and wine, and ordered him to ascend his ancestors' tombs.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Sui and Ma Chao revolted in the west, Cao Cao posted Xu Huang at Fenyin to steady Hedong, gave him oxen and wine for sacrifice, and had him visit his ancestors' graves.

sentences.zh: 太祖至潼关，恐不得渡，召问晃。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor reached Tong Pass, he feared being unable to cross and summoned Huang to ask him.
translations.idiomatic: At Tong Pass, fearing he could not force the crossing, Cao Cao called Xu Huang in for counsel.

sentences.zh: 晃曰：“公盛兵於此，而贼不复别守蒲阪，知其无谋也。

translations.literal: Huang said: "The lord masses troops here, yet the bandits do not again separately guard Puban—I know they lack planning.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huang said, "You have massed the army here while the enemy leaves Puban unguarded—they have no strategy.

sentences.zh: 今假臣精兵

translations.literal: Now if you lend me picked troops
translations.idiomatic: Lend me picked troops

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之云：案晃于时未应称臣，传写者误也。〉

translations.literal: 〈Your servant Songzhi says: examining Huang, at that time he ought not to have called himself 'subject'; the copyist erred.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Pei Songzhi notes that Xu Huang would not have said "your servant" here—the text is corrupt.〉

sentences.zh: 渡蒲坂津，为军先置，以截其里，贼可擒也。

translations.literal: to cross the Puban ford, act as the army's vanguard, and thereby cut their rear—the bandits can be captured.
translations.idiomatic: to cross at Puban, seize the bridgehead, and cut them off—we can take them.

sentences.zh: ”太祖曰：“善。

translations.literal: " The Grand Progenitor said: "Good.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao said, "Good.

sentences.zh: ”使晃以步骑四千人渡津。

translations.literal: " He ordered Huang with four thousand foot and horse to cross the ford.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered Xu Huang to take four thousand mixed troops across the ford.

sentences.zh: 作堑栅未成，贼梁兴夜将步骑五千餘人攻晃，晃击走之，太祖军得渡。

translations.literal: The moat and palisade were not yet finished when the bandit Liang Xing by night led more than five thousand foot and horse to attack Huang; Huang struck and routed them, and the Grand Progenitor's army was able to cross.
translations.idiomatic: Before his trenches and stockade were complete, Liang Xing attacked by night with five thousand men; Xu Huang drove him off and opened the crossing for Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 遂破超等，使晃与夏侯渊平隃麋、汧诸氐，与太祖会安定。

translations.literal: Thereupon they defeated Chao and others; he ordered Huang together with Xiahou Yuan to pacify the Di of Yumi and Qian, and to join the Grand Progenitor at Anding.
translations.idiomatic: After Ma Chao's defeat he sent Xu Huang with Xiahou Yuan to pacify the Di of Yumi and Qian and join Cao Cao at Anding.

sentences.zh: 太祖还鄴，使晃与夏侯渊平鄜、夏阳餘贼，斩梁兴，降三千餘户。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor returned to Ye and ordered Huang together with Xiahou Yuan to pacify the remaining bandits of Fu and Xiayang, beheaded Liang Xing, and caused more than three thousand households to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Ye he sent Xu Huang with Xiahou Yuan to mop up bandits in Fu and Xiayang, beheaded Liang Xing, and brought in more than three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 从征张鲁。

translations.literal: He followed in campaigning against Zhang Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the expedition against Zhang Lu.

sentences.zh: 别遣晃讨攻椟、仇夷诸山氐，皆降之。

translations.literal: Separately he dispatched Huang to campaign against the mountain Di of Gongdu (椟), Qiuyi, and others; all caused them to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He detached Xu Huang to subdue the mountain Di around the Gongdu and Qiuyi ranges (as named in the text), all of whom submitted.

sentences.zh: 迁平寇将军。

translations.literal: He was promoted to general who pacifies bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general who pacifies bandits.

sentences.zh: 解将军张顺围。

translations.literal: He relieved General Zhang Shun's siege.
translations.idiomatic: He lifted the siege of General Zhang Shun.

sentences.zh: 击贼陈福等三十餘屯，皆破之。

translations.literal: He struck the bandits Chen Fu and others, more than thirty encampments, and in all defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed more than thirty camps of bandits led by Chen Fu and the like.

sentences.zh: 太祖还鄴，留晃与夏侯渊拒刘备於阳平。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor returned to Ye, left Huang together with Xiahou Yuan to resist Liu Bei at Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao returned to Ye he left Xu Huang with Xiahou Yuan to hold Liu Bei at Yangping.

sentences.zh: 备遣陈式等十餘营绝马鸣阁道，晃别征破之，贼自投山谷，多死者。

translations.literal: Bei dispatched Chen Shi and more than ten camps to cut off the Mamming pavilion road; Huang separately campaigned and defeated them; the bandits themselves threw themselves into valleys and gorges, and many died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei sent Chen Shi with a dozen camps to sever the Mamming defile; Xu Huang attacked on a separate axis, routed them, and many of the enemy plunged to their deaths in the gorges.

sentences.zh: 太祖闻，甚喜，假晃节，令曰：“此阁道，汉中之险要咽喉也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor heard it and was very pleased; he lent Huang the credential insignia and ordered, saying: "This pavilion road is Hanzhong's critical throat.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Cao Cao gave Xu Huang the baton and wrote, "This defile is the throat of Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 刘备欲断绝外内，以取汉中。

translations.literal: Liu Bei wishes to sever outer from inner in order to take Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei means to cut the interior off from the outside and seize Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 将军一举，克夺贼计，善之善者也。

translations.literal: The general in one stroke was able to seize away the bandits' plan—of good, the best.
translations.idiomatic: In one stroke you have spoiled their design—excellent in the highest degree.

sentences.zh: ”太祖遂自至阳平，引出汉中诸军。

translations.literal: " The Grand Progenitor thereupon personally came to Yangping and led out the various armies of Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao then came to Yangping in person and withdrew the Hanzhong armies.

sentences.zh: 复遣晃助曹仁讨关羽，屯宛。

translations.literal: Again he dispatched Huang to assist Cao Ren in campaigning against Guan Yu and garrison Wan.
translations.idiomatic: He again sent Xu Huang to aid Cao Ren against Guan Yu, with headquarters at Wan.

sentences.zh: 会汉水暴隘，于禁等没。

translations.literal: It happened that the Han River suddenly rose in flood (text 隘 may stand for 溢), and Yu Jin and others were submerged.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Han River burst its banks in a sudden flood and Yu Jin's entire command was swallowed.

sentences.zh: 羽围仁於樊，又围将军吕常於襄阳。

translations.literal: Yu besieged Ren at Fan and again besieged General Lü Chang at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu besieged Cao Ren at Fan and General Lü Chang at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 晃所将多新卒，以羽难与争锋，遂前至阳陵陂屯。

translations.literal: Those Huang led were mostly new recruits; because Yu was hard to contend with at the point, he thereupon advanced to garrison at Yangling Slope.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huang's men were largely raw levies, and Guan Yu was too formidable to meet head-on, so he halted first at Yangling Slope.

sentences.zh: 太祖复还，遣将军徐商、吕建等诣晃，令曰：“须兵马集至，乃俱前。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor returned again, dispatched Generals Xu Shang, Lü Jian, and others to go to Huang, and ordered, saying: "Wait until troops and horses are gathered and arrived, then advance together.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao returned he sent Xu Shang, Lü Jian, and others to Xu Huang with orders to wait until all forces had joined before advancing together.

sentences.zh: ”贼屯偃城。

translations.literal: " The bandits garrisoned Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: " The enemy held Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 晃到，诡道作都堑，示欲截其后，贼烧屯走。

translations.literal: When Huang arrived, he by deceitful roads made capital moats, showing an intent to cut off their rear; the bandits burned the camps and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huang arrived and dug long trenches as if to cut off the enemy's retreat; they burned their camps and fled.

sentences.zh: 晃得偃城，两面连营，稍前，去贼围三丈所。

translations.literal: Huang obtained Yancheng, on two sides linked camps, gradually advanced forward, and was about three zhang from the bandits' siege.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huang took Yancheng, linked camps on both flanks, edged forward until he stood within a few yards of Guan Yu's siege lines.

sentences.zh: 未攻，太祖前后遣殷署、硃盖等凡十二营诣晃。

translations.literal: Before attacking, the Grand Progenitor before and after dispatched Yin Shu, Zhu Gai, and others, in all twelve camps, to go to Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Before he struck, Cao Cao sent twelve reinforcement camps under Yin Shu, Zhu Gai, and others to join Xu Huang.

sentences.zh: 贼围头有屯，又别屯四冢。

translations.literal: The bandits at Weitou had an encampment, and again separately encamped at Four Mounds.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy held Weitou and had a separate force at the Four Mounds.

sentences.zh: 晃扬声当攻围头屯，而密攻四冢。

translations.literal: Huang loudly proclaimed he would attack the Weitou encampment, but secretly attacked the Four Mounds.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huang feinted toward Weitou but struck the Four Mounds in secret.

sentences.zh: 羽见四冢欲坏，自将步骑五千出战，晃击之，退走，遂追陷与俱入围，破之，或自投沔水死。

translations.literal: When Yu saw the Four Mounds about to be ruined, he personally led five thousand foot and horse to give battle; Huang struck them, they retreated and fled, thereupon pursued, broke in together with them into the siege, defeated them, and some threw themselves into the Mian River and died.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the Four Mounds about to fall, Guan Yu led five thousand men out; Xu Huang drove them back, pursued them into the siege ring, broke their formation, and many drowned themselves in the Han River.

sentences.zh: 太祖令曰：“贼围堑鹿角十重，将军致战全胜，遂陷贼围，多斩首虏。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor ordered, saying: "The bandits' siege moats and deer-horn abatis are ten layers deep; the general brought battle to complete victory, thereupon broke into the bandits' siege ring and beheaded and captured many.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao issued an order: "The foe had ten rings of ditch and abatis; you fought through to total victory, broke into their siege, and took a heavy toll of heads and prisoners.

sentences.zh: 吾用兵三十餘年，及所闻古之善用兵者，未有长驱径入敌围者也。

translations.literal: I have used troops for more than thirty years, and reaching those I have heard of among the ancients skilled at using troops, there has never been one who long-drove straight entered the enemy siege ring.
translations.idiomatic: In more than thirty years of campaigning, and in everything I have read of the masters of war, I have never seen a long drive straight through an enemy cordon like yours.

sentences.zh: 且樊、襄阳之在围，过於莒、即墨，将军之功，逾孙武、穰苴。

translations.literal: Moreover Fan and Xiangyang in siege surpass Ju and Jimo; the general's merit exceeds Sun Wu and Rangju.
translations.idiomatic: The sieges of Fan and Xiangyang were graver than those of Ju and Jimo; your achievement outshines Sun Wu and Tian Rangju.

sentences.zh: ”晃振旅还摩陂，太祖迎晃七里，置酒大会。

translations.literal: " Huang shook the brigades and returned to Mopi; the Grand Progenitor welcomed Huang for seven li and set out wine for a great gathering.
translations.idiomatic: " Xu Huang marched back to Mopi; Cao Cao rode seven li to meet him and gave a great banquet.

sentences.zh: 太祖举卮酒劝晃，且劳之曰：“全樊、襄阳，将军之功也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor raised a goblet of wine to urge Huang on, and consoled him, saying: "The preservation of Fan and Xiangyang is the general's merit.
translations.idiomatic: He raised a cup to Xu Huang and said, "The relief of Fan and Xiangyang is your doing.

sentences.zh: ”时诸军皆集，太祖案行诸营，士卒咸离陈观，而晃军营整齐，将士驻陈不动。

translations.literal: " At that time the various armies were all assembled; the Grand Progenitor inspected the various camps; soldiers all left formation to watch, but Huang's army camp was neat and orderly, officers and troops stationed in formation without moving.
translations.idiomatic: " When the hosts had gathered and Cao Cao toured the camps, men everywhere broke ranks to stare—only Xu Huang's formation stood motionless in perfect order.

sentences.zh: 太祖叹曰：“徐将军可谓有周亚夫之风矣。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor sighed and said: "General Xu may be said to have the manner of Zhou Yafu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sighed, "General Xu has the stamp of Zhou Yafu.

sentences.zh: 文帝即王位，以晃为右将军，进封逯乡侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen assumed the kingly throne, he appointed Huang general of the right and advanced his enfeoffment to marquis of Luxiang canton.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Pi assumed the kingship he named Xu Huang general of the right and raised his fief to marquis of Luxiang township.

sentences.zh: 及践阼，进封杨侯。

translations.literal: When he ascended the imperial steps, he advanced the enfeoffment to Marquis Yang.
translations.idiomatic: At his accession he promoted the fief to marquis of Yang.

sentences.zh: 与夏侯尚讨刘备於上庸，破之。

translations.literal: Together with Xiahou Shang he campaigned against Liu Bei at Shangyong and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: With Xiahou Shang he defeated Liu Bei at Shangyong.

sentences.zh: 以晃镇阳平，徙封阳平侯。

translations.literal: He used Huang to garrison Yangping and transferred the enfeoffment to Marquis Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: He stationed Xu Huang at Yangping and transferred his title to marquis of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，拒吴将诸葛瑾於襄阳。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming assumed the throne, he resisted Wu general Zhuge Jin at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he held Zhuge Jin of Wu at bay at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 增邑二百，并前三千一百户。

translations.literal: His fief was increased by two hundred households; together with the previous it was three thousand one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred more households were added, for three thousand one hundred in all.

sentences.zh: 病笃，遗令敛以时服。

translations.literal: When his illness was grave, he left instructions to be encoffined in seasonal dress.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he ordered a plain burial in everyday clothes.

sentences.zh: 性俭约畏慎，将军常远斥候，先为不可胜，然后战，追奔争利，士不暇食。

translations.literal: By nature frugal and cautious in awe, as general he always sent scouts far, first made himself unable to be defeated, then fought; pursuing the routed and contending for advantage, the troops had no leisure to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Frugal and watchful by nature, he habitually pushed scouts far ahead, secured an unassailable position before he would fight, and in hot pursuit for advantage drove his men until they had no time to eat.

sentences.zh: 常叹曰：“古人患不遭明君，今幸遇之，常以功自效，何用私誉为！

translations.literal: He often sighed and said: "The ancients worried at not meeting an enlightened lord; now I am fortunate to meet one; I always use merit to repay him—what use is private reputation!
translations.idiomatic: He would say, "The ancients feared they would never find a worthy lord; I have found one, and I mean to repay him with deeds—what need have I of empty fame?

sentences.zh: ”终不广交援。

translations.literal: " In the end he did not widely make friends and connections.
translations.idiomatic: " He never courted a wide circle of patrons.

sentences.zh: 太和元年薨，谥曰壮侯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taihe he died; his posthumous title was Marquis Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Taihe 1 and was posthumously titled Marquis Zhuang, "the Stalwart."

sentences.zh: 子盖嗣。

translations.literal: The son Gai inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xu Gai inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 盖薨，子霸嗣。

translations.literal: When Gai died, the son Ba inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Gai died, his son Xu Ba succeeded.

sentences.zh: 明帝分晃户，封晃子孙二人列侯。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming divided Huang's households and enfeoffed two of Huang's grandsons and sons as full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming divided Xu Huang's fief and enfeoffed two of his descendants as full marquises.

translations.literal: 【Appraisal (section rubric).】
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal.

sentences.zh: 评曰：太祖建兹武功，而时之良将，五子为先。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: The Grand Progenitor established these martial achievements, and among the fine generals of the time, the five sons came first.
translations.idiomatic: The historian's appraisal runs: In the martial enterprise that Cao Cao raised, the foremost commanders of the age were these five.

sentences.zh: 于禁最号毅重，然弗克其终。

translations.literal: Yu Jin was most called resolute and weighty, yet he could not master his end.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin bore the reputation of stern steadfastness, yet he could not bring his career to an honorable close.

sentences.zh: 张郃以巧变为称，乐进以骁果显名，而鉴其行事，未副所闻。

translations.literal: Zhang He by clever adaptation was praised; Yue Jin by fierce resolution displayed fame; yet examining their deeds and conduct, they did not match what was heard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang He was famed for resourceful adaptation, Yue Jin for fierce daring, yet their recorded deeds fall somewhat short of their reputations.

sentences.zh: 或注记有遗漏，未如张辽、徐晃之备详也。

translations.literal: Perhaps the notes and records had omissions and lacunae, and were not as complete and detailed as for Zhang Liao and Xu Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps the compilers omitted material; at any rate the accounts are not as full as those for Zhang Liao and Xu Huang.
